card: This pull request adds an optional sat_vb boolean option to getmempoolinfo, getnetworkinfo, estimatesmartfee, and estimaterawfee, allowing callers to receive feerates in sat/vB instead of legacy BTC/kvB. It addresses developer friction and potential rounding errors from client-side conversions in sub-1 sat/vB environments. Feerates in sat/vB are formatted to three decimal places via a new ValueFromFeeRate helper, and options are exposed as both dictionary fields and top-level named arguments. The change is part of tracking issue #32093 and has no external dependencies.
changed_since_previous: Added standalone release notes snippet in doc/release-notes-33741.md and expanded named argument handling/testing across the modified RPC methods.
evidence: PR description notes that 'Returning feerates in BTC/kvB it can be very burdensome and is not good practice, as the most widely adopted units are sat/vB.' (referencing issue #32093)

PR description highlights precision risks: 'Because of sub 1sat/vB environment we cannot rely on GetFee() because it internally uses FeeFrac EvaluateFee() function which rounds the values to always return an int. If the feerate < 1 then it will be rounded to 1 or 0.'
problem: Bitcoin Core fee RPCs return values exclusively in BTC/kvB, whereas modern tooling, wallets, and user interfaces almost universally operate in sat/vB. Downstream clients must manually convert units, adding client-side arithmetic that can suffer precision loss or integer truncation under low-fee (sub-1 sat/vB) conditions.

risk.why: Mistakes in RPC parameter parsing or output formatting could alter RPC response structures and break downstream applications or automation.

scope_notes: Touches four distinct RPC endpoints across mempool, net, and fee estimation files, introducing a new UniValue formatting helper in core_io and client convert parameter entries.
summary: Adds an optional `sat_vb` boolean option to `getmempoolinfo`, `getnetworkinfo`, `estimatesmartfee`, and `estimaterawfee`, allowing callers to receive feerates formatted in sat/vB rather than BTC/kvB. Introduces a `ValueFromFeeRate` helper in `core_io` that formats feerates with three decimal places of precision, avoiding integer rounding issues in sub-1 sat/vB environments. Also adjusts RPC conversion tables and parsing so `sat_vb` and existing estimator options can be passed as named arguments.
